Bobrovyy Kut Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kherson Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Bobrovyy Kut was founded in 1807 as a Jewish agricultural colony by settlers from the Mogilev Governorate, later becoming part of the Kalinindorf Jewish National Raion, documented elsewhere in this collection. About 400 Jews who remained after some managed to evacuate were murdered here in September 1941, alongside Jews from other communities. According to local resident Anatoly Ivanovich, born in 1937, the cemetery was demolished when farms were built here around the 1950s; his wife, who is half-Jewish, was the only person in the village to survive the German invasion. A mass grave in the village is known locally as 'the well.'
